_README: MULTILINGUAL NAME SWAP (Stage 6; scripts/per_token_map.py --swap-file, slurm/16_name_swap_ml.sbatch).
WHY. At equal learned-model certainty (p > 0.999), each language's own unlearning destroyed
0% of copied-name tokens in fr/en/id but 50% in ru and 96% in ja. Ruled out: spelling
mismatch, retain-set overlap of name pieces, lower copy rates in ru/ja retain answers.
Leading explanation, TWO SUPPORTS: the Latin-script name is backed by copying AND by the
French learning of exactly those tokens (recalled names, facts 0/20: learned p = 1.00 in
fr/en/id, 0.05 / 0.09 in ru/ja); the transliterated name by copying only. That rests on
2 facts and is confounded with script. This file removes the name from the 38 questions
in en / id / ru / ja (the answer is unchanged), so for every name token we get its
LEARNED SUPPORT = how well the learned model recalls it with no name to copy. The test is
WITHIN a language: do copied-name tokens with more learned support survive that language's
own unlearning more often? Within one script, so script cannot be the explanation.
VARIANTS: orig (unchanged question, re-scored in the same run) and A (the name replaced by
a birth-date description -- the identifier facts 0 and 20 teach; no city, so no part of
the surname leaks). French has its own file (name_swap_questions.json, variants A/B/C).
PLACEHOLDERS. {D} = the description. Russian needs the description in the case the
sentence demands: {N} nominative, {G} genitive (also the animate accusative), {I}
instrumental; templates add the closing comma a mid-sentence participle phrase needs.
Wording follows each language's own (pass-2) question; only the name phrase is replaced,
except where a possessive or doubled 'born' forced a rephrase (en/id/ru/ja fact 2, en
possessives -> 'of {D}', id 30/35, ja 2).
Hand-written 2026-10-11. Russian and Japanese should be checked by a fluent reader; the
dry run prints all of them.
